enriched.title: Present Perfect e Vocabulário de Física e Ações Cotidianas
enriched.summary: A aula aborda o uso do Present Perfect com palavras relacionadas a experiências e situações cotidianas, além de introduzir vocabulário específico sobre física e ações do dia a dia. O foco também inclui a diferenciação entre 'been to' e 'gone to'.
mainTopics: Vocabulário de Física e Ações Cotidianas

vocabulary.definition: The physical substance that occupies space and possesses mass.
examples: Matter is anything that occupies space and has mass.

vocabulary.definition: Something that exists outside the physical substance of matter.
examples: Some theories in physics discuss what lies beyond matter.

vocabulary.definition: To turn around quickly in a circular motion.
examples: She spun the globe, and pointed to Latin America.

vocabulary.definition: To change the direction or shape of something.
examples: Light rays bend as they pass from air to water.

vocabulary.definition: To determine the size, amount, or degree of something.
examples: Scientists measure the speed of light to study the universe.

vocabulary.translation: um ao outro, um do outro
vocabulary.definition: Used to show mutual actions or feelings.
examples: The two companies are in competition with each other.

vocabulary.definition: Unable to think clearly or understand something.
examples: My grandpa gets very confused sometimes.
The river flows through the valley.

vocabulary.definition: An informal shortening of the word 'through'.
examples: He went tru the door quickly.

grammar.explanation: The Present Perfect is used to describe actions or situations that happened at an unspecified time in the past or have a connection to the present.
rules: Do not use specific time expressions like 'yesterday' or 'last year' with Present Perfect.
examples: My mother has baked a cake.
I have eaten all the food.
commonMistakes: Using a specific time expression: 'I have eaten yesterday.' (Incorrect)
Forgetting the auxiliary verb: 'She baked a cake.' (Incorrect for Present Perfect)

grammar.explanation: 'Been to' is used when someone has visited a place and returned, while 'Gone to' is used when someone is currently at the place or has not returned yet.
rules: 'Gone to' indicates someone is still at the location or on their way.
examples: I have been to Japan, but I’ve never visited South Korea.
She has gone to the supermarket to buy some milk.
commonMistakes: Mixing up the two: 'I have gone to Japan.' (Incorrect if you are back.)

practiceQuestions.question: I know the way to the museum. I __________ there many times before.
practiceQuestions.explanation: 'Been to' is used for completed visits and returning.

practiceQuestions.question: Where is your sister? She isn't in her room. — She __________ the supermarket to buy some milk.
practiceQuestions.explanation: 'Gone to' is used because she has not returned yet.

culturalNotes: The difference between 'been to' and 'gone to' can be tricky for non-native speakers, but it is commonly used in English-speaking countries to clarify someone's location.
studyTips: Practice using 'been to' and 'gone to' in sentences about your own experiences.
Learn irregular verbs by grouping them based on similar patterns.
originalExamples: She spun the globe, and pointed to Latin America. (Ela girou o globo e apontou para a América Latina.)
Light rays bend as they pass from air to water. (Os raios de luz se curvam ao passar do ar para a água.)
The two companies are in competition with each other. (As duas empresas estão em competição uma com a outra.)
My grandpa gets very confused sometimes. (Meu avô fica muito confuso às vezes.)

warnings: practiceQuestions tem apenas 2 item(ns), recomendado mínimo de 3
